(AMD), speaks during the company's Gamers Day event in Seoul, South Korea, on Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026. \n\nSeongJoon Cho | Bloomberg | Getty Images\n\nAdvanced Micro Devices Add To Watchlist reported third-quarter earnings on Tuesday that beat Wall Street's expectations, with revenue jumping 45% and data center sales nearly doubling from a year earlier. The stock was up 8% in extended trading, but later pared those gains as election results came in.\n\nHere's how the chipmaker did versus LSEG consensus estimates for the quarter:\n\n- Earnings per share: $2.09 adjusted vs. $1.95 expected\n- Revenue: $13.38 billion vs. $13.09 billion expected\n\nRevenue increased from $9.25 billion a year earlier, AMD said in a statement. Neoclouds like CoreWeave Add To Watchlist and Nebius Add To Watchlist rallied earlier Tuesday and remained higher after AMD reported results.\n\nCEO Lisa Su said on the earnings call that she expects server revenue to double year over year in 2027 and data center AI growth to accelerate even faster than the company had projected 90 days ago. The company expects data center to drive the majority of its revenue and earnings growth.\n\n\"We have worked across our supply chain to secure the wafers, substrates, advanced packaging, memory, and other key components needed to support much higher growth next year,\" Su said on the earnings call.\n\nAMD's report comes days after Intel Add To Watchlist disclosed similar data center growth, with revenue in that segment up 78% in the third quarter. But Intel's stock plummeted 29% on Friday over concerns about weak guidance and Intel's ability to meet demand. \n\nThe data center unit makes up the majority of AMD's business, accounting for 64% of overall revenue, up from 47% a year ago.\n\nAfter years spent chasing Nvidia in the market for artificial intelligence graphics processing units, or GPUs, AMD's central processing units, or CPUs, are experiencing a major resurgence with the rise of agentic AI apps like Meta Add To Watchlist 's Muse. AMD's server CPUs are key for agentic apps because they power virtual machines and can run for hours on their own. Demand from agentic AI boosted AMD shares to a record in October.\n\n\"Adoption is just starting, and we expect demand to grow sharply as agents are deployed more broadly and take on more complex work,\" Su said on the earnings call with analysts. \n\nAMD stock chart.\n\n## PC market struggles\n\nAMD's stock is up about 125% this year, but it saw three consecutive days of losses before rallying on Tuesday amid an industrywide sell-off tied to fears about overspending on AI. \n\nAMD is also a major player in the weakening PC market, which Intel blamed for its poor outlook last week. AMD and Intel are the largest makers of traditional x86 processors that power many laptops and desktops, while other laptops rely on Arm Add To Watchlist -based processors from the likes of Qualcomm Add To Watchlist and Apple.\n\nGlobal PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier due to soaring costs for memory and other components, according to Counterpoint Research.\n\nAMD reports PC chip sales in a segment combined with gaming chips. Revenue in that business fell 8% from a year earlier to $3.7 billion. Gaming revenue was down 40% from a year ago. \n\nFor the fourth quarter, AMD said it expects about $17 billion in revenue, beating the $16.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AMD sees its gross margin for the quarter coming in at 55%, slightly below the average estimate of 55.3%, according to StreetAccount.\n\nAMD also sells data center GPUs and full rack-scale systems called Helios that compete directly with Nvidia's Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems. Meta, Microsoft Add To Watchlist, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Oracle Add To Watchlist are all beginning to use AMD Helios in their data centers. Meta said last week that its Helios racks are up and running, and AMD agreed to invest $1 billion in Meta's equity offering.\n\nAMD has also committed to investing up to $5 billion in Anthropic, which unveiled its highly anticipated prospectus last week as it inches closer to a potentially historic initial public offering.\n\nDuring a visit to Taiwan in October, Su said she plans to \"substantially increase our supply in 2027.\" Su and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang have both made ","highlights":["CEO Lisa Su said on the earnings call that she expects server revenue to double year over year in 2027 and data center AI growth to accelerate even faster than the company had projected 90 days ago. (AMD)\n\n# AMD Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results\n\n November 03, 2026 4:15 pm EST Download as PDF \n\nAMD delivers record quarter as Data Center segment revenue grows 97% year-over-year, driven by record sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs\n\nSANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue was $13.4 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.8 billion, net income was $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.46. On a non-GAAP (*) basis, gross margin was 56%, operating income was $3.9 billion, net income was $3.5 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.09.\n\n“We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year,” said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. “Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and ‘Venice’ production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years.”\n\n“Third quarter revenue grew 45% year-over-year to a record $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 74%, demonstrating the significant operating leverage in our business model as our Data Center business drives scale,” said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. “Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our Data Center portfolio.”\n\nGAAP Quarterly Financial Results\n\n| | Q3'26 | Q3'25 | Y/Y | Q2'26 | Q/Q |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| GPUs. \n- Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors. Gaming business revenue was $773 million, down 40% year-over-year, due to lower semi-custom and graphics revenue.\n- Embedded segment revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29% year-over-year, led by growth in aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets. \n\nRecent Highlights \n\n- AMD solutions and software are powering superintelligence infrastructure at scale: \n\n- AMD EPYC CPUs.\n- HPE announced that Vultr will deploy the first AMD Helios by HPE systems.\n- Oracle Cloud Infrastructure announced its OCI Compute E7 cloud compute instances will be powered by 6 th Gen AMD EPYC CPUs, supporting enterprise applications and the CPU services surrounding models.\n- AMD introduced the AMD Helion reference architecture, an open, flexible blueprint for building rack-scale agentic systems that lets customers configure the mix of CPUs and GPUs based on their workloads.\n- AMD ROCm™ 10 was released, bringing AI-native developer experiences to AMD platforms with ROCm.AI, along with performance improvements and updated libraries, compilers, frameworks, tools and model support.\n- The EuroHPC JU selected AMD Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6 th Gen AMD EPYC processors Cherney and Stephen Nellis\n\nNov 3 (Reuters) - AMD forecast faster-than-expected 2027 growth as its data-center sales surge and its multibillion-dollar challenge to Nvidia gathers pace, sending its shares up 8% in extended trading.\n\nThe forecast and market-beating third-quarter results offered a strong counterpoint on Tuesday to mounting fears that the AI boom is losing steam and soothed investor concerns after rival Intel issued a weak outlook last week.\n\nIntel’s shares rose 2%, Nvidia stock climbed over 1% and Broadcom also advanced 1.2%.\n\nOn a conference call with analysts, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects overall revenue to rise more than 80% in 2027. Su’s forecast is higher than the 77% growth analysts estimate, according to LSEG data.\n\nSu told analysts that 80% of sales next year will come from data-center chips that will \"drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth.\"\n\n\"We see demand across the data-center business, across our CPU business, as well as our data-center AI business,\" Su said. \"And when you look at the rate and pace of that growth, we’ve been planning for it for the last several years.\"\n\nData-center revenue jumped 97% to a record $8.55 billion in the third quarter, exceeding estimates of $8.20 billion.\n\nThe company expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, above analysts’ average estimate of $16.23 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG.\n\nAMD’s line of chips is positioned to benefit from the massive AI data-center buildout, portfolio manager at Gabelli Funds Hendi Susanto said.\n\n\"The stock’s resilience despite broader pressure on AI-related names suggests investors see AMD’s results as confirming its technology leadership and its strong position to keep gaining market share,\" he added.\n\nAMD is benefiting as a shift in AI workloads toward running models in real-world applications drives demand for its graphics processing units and central processors.\n\n\"The AMD numbers provide a greatly needed boost both for AI infrastructure and even, to a smaller degree, the PC market,\" chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research Bob O’Donnell said.\n\nThe company’s adjusted gross margin is expected to be about 55%, in line with estimates of 55.27% and down from 56% in the third quarter.\n\nRAMPING UP AI ROLLOUTS\n\nAMD has stepped up AI product rollouts, moving beyond standalone chips to compete with Nvidia’s rack-scale systems.\n\nThe company’s flagship Helios rack, combining its MI455X accelerator and new \"Venice\" server chips, is in production and set for a larger ramp-up in the fourth quarter. The initial systems are being tested at Meta.\n\nAMD’s third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $13.38 billion, beating estimates of $13.09 billion.\n\nAdjusted profit came in at $2.09 per share, compared with estimates of $1.95.\n\nThe semiconductor industry is also grappling with a global memory shortage, leaving expensive high-bandwidth memory used in AI processors in scarce supply as manufacturers race to increase production.\n\nThird-quarter sales in AMD’s client and gaming segment, home to its PC chips and console processors, fell 8% to $3.72 billion, missing estimates of $3.79 billion.\n\nAMD said it expects PC unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage next year, though Su said the company would \"outperform the market.\"\n\nLast week, Intel forecast its chip revenue to decline in the mid-20% range for its fourth quarter and the slowdown would last into 2027.\n\n## Latest comments\n\n| Name | Last | Chg. % | Vol. |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| FIS | 29.64 | -23.99% | 13.85M |\n| TRMB | 53.72 | -18.12% | 1.71M |\n| VST | 118.50 | -15.11% | 8.52M |\n| DDOG | 188.91 | -14.33% | 5.22M |\n| PWR | 568.18 | -13.52% | 963.97K |\n| NRG | 83.74 | -13.01% | 2.84M |\n| GNRC | 182.22 | -12.93% | 664.74K |\n\n| Name | Last | Chg. % | Vol. |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| AMD | 482.70 | -0.25% | 27.68M |\n| NVDA | 202.21 | -2.17% | 50.03M |\n| INTC | 57.42 | -5.17% | 65.12M |\n| MU | 802.08 | -6.20% | 13.63M |\n| SPCX | 136.29 | -3.55% | 64.67M |","highlights":["Nov 3 (Reuters) - AMD forecast faster-than-expected 2027 growth as its data-center sales surge and its multibillion-dollar challenge to Nvidia gathers pace, sending its shares up 8% in extended trading.\n\n...\n\nOn a conference call with analysts, AMD CEO Lisa Su said the company expects overall revenue to rise more than 80% in 2027. It expects December-quarter guidance of $17 billion, compared with the Street’s $16.3 billion forecast. \n\nHowever, the main focus will be on the longer-term outlook, particularly revenue from server central processing units (CPUs) and artificial intelligence graphics processing units (GPUs). \n\nWall Street expects AMD’s data center revenue to exceed $70 billion in 2027, while buy-side expectations are closer to $80 billion to $90 billion. Jefferies sees scope for consensus estimates to rise to around $75 billion after the results, although it does not expect AMD to meet the more optimistic forecasts in a single quarter. \n\nThe broker forecasts $42 billion in AI revenue for 2027, with potential to reach $48 billion if AMD ships 14,000 racks. However, constraints in logic chip and memory supply, alongside limits on data centre power and infrastructure, could restrict growth. \n\nAMD’s Venice server CPUs and MI450 GPUs will also compete for capacity on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co’s N2 process node, creating potential trade-offs between CPU and GPU production. Jefferies expects AMD to favour GPUs because of their higher gross profit potential per wafer. \n\nThe broker remains positive on AMD’s fundamentals, citing growing interest in AI CPUs and the planned fourth-quarter ramp-up of its Helios rack-scale computing platform. It cautioned that initial deployments could face delays. \n\nValuation is another concern. AMD trades at 16 to 20 times Jefferies’ bullish 2028 earnings-per-share estimate of $30 to $35, leaving execution critical to its investment case. \n\nAMD is scheduled to report results after the market close on November 3. Key points:\n\n- Revenue outlook: AMD expected to beat quarterly estimates; Jefferies forecasts AI-related revenue of about $42B for 2027, with potential to reach $48B if AMD ships 14,000 racks.\n- Growth constraints: Supply limits for logic chips and memory, plus data center power and infrastructure bottlenecks, could cap upside in the near term.\n- Capacity and trade-offs: AMD’s Venice server CPUs and MI450 GPUs will compete for capacity on TSMC’s N2 node, potentially forcing choices between CPU and GPU production. Jefferies believes GPUs offer higher gross profit per wafer, which may steer production.\n- Positives and risks: Fundamentals remain favorable due to rising AI CPU interest and the Helios rack-scale platform ramp (targeting Q4). Initial deployments of Helios may face delays.\n- Helios and MI450: The plan includes Helios rack-scale computing ramp in Q4 and MI450 GPU availability, with execution risk in early deployments.\n\nOverall takeaway: Strong AI demand backdrop for AMD with meaningful long-term AI revenue potential, but near-term supply, capacity allocation, and deployment delays could limit immediate upside. Emerging focus areas include Helios ramp and MI450 deployment, plus balancing CPU/GPU manufacturing on limited node Transcribing","text":"AMD (AMD) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript | The Motley Fool\n\n# AMD (AMD) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript\n\nData center sales nearly doubled as AI demand pushed supply to its limits this quarter.\n\nBy Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 4, 2026 at 10:24AM EST\n\nImage source: The Motley Fool.\n\n## DATE\n\nTuesday, Nov. 3, 2026\n\n## CALL PARTICIPANTS\n\n- VP, Financial Strategy and IR - Matt Ramsay\n- Chair and CEO - Lisa Su\n- Executive Vice President, CFO and Treasurer - Jean Hu\n\n## TAKEAWAYS\n\n- Revenue -- $13.4 billion, representing 45% year-over-year growth driven by record sales of EPYC and Instinct products.\n- Non-GAAP EPS -- $2.09, increasing 74% year over year as profitability growth outpaced top-line expansion.\n- Data Center Revenue -- $8.5 billion, a 97% year-over-year increase fueled by cloud and enterprise server sales more than doubling.\n- Data Center Revenue Mix -- 64% of total revenue, up from 47% one year ago as the company shifts toward infrastructure compute.\n- Non-GAAP Gross Margin -- 56%, an increase of 190 basis points year over year reflecting a richer mix of data center products.\n- Non-GAAP Operating Margin -- 29%, expanding 5 percentage points year over year due to operating leverage in the business.\n- Q4 Revenue Guidance -- $17 billion at the midpoint, representing 66% year-over-year growth driven by data center segment acceleration.\n- FY2027 Revenue Growth -- Over 80%, which management noted is more than twice the rate of the long-term financial model.\n- Embedded Revenue -- $1.1 billion, growing 29% year over year with design wins on track to exceed $18 billion in 2026.\n- Client Revenue -- $2.9 billion, a 7% year-over-year increase supported by Ryzen mobile processor sales.\n- Gaming Revenue -- $773 million, a 40% year-over-year decline due to lower semi-custom console sales and graphics demand.\n- Inventory -- $11.5 billion, an increase of $3 billion sequentially to support rapid data center product ramps and secured capacity.\n- Cash and Short-Term Investments -- $15.8 billion, following a $4.75 billion senior notes offering completed in Aug. 2026.\n- Server CPU TAM -- Approximately $220 billion by 2030, according to management projections for the total addressable market.\n- Venice Platform Adoption -- Over 240 platforms committed by partners, representing a 20% increase compared to the previous Turin generation.\n- MI455X Shipments -- Volume shipments commenced in the quarter to customers including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, and OpenAI.\n- Data Center Operating Income -- $2.9 billion, up 168% year over year as operating margins in the segment reached 34%.\n- PC Market Unit Shipments -- Management expects the total market to decline by a double-digit percentage in 2027.\n- Operating Expenses -- $3.6 billion, a 29% year-over-year increase driven by R&D investments in data center silicon and software.\n- Free Cash Flow -- $554 million, reflecting increased working capital investments and capital expenditures for back-end capacity.\n\nNeed a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected] \n\n## RISKS\n\n- Su stated, \"PC sell-through slowed late in the quarter as higher memory and component costs weighed on demand,\" suggesting pricing pressures in consumer segments.\n- Su warned that the company expects PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage in 2027, which may impact client segment performance.\n- Hu indicated that \"quarterly noncash fair value adjustments are expected to increase\" related to customer warrants, which will fluctuate based on the company's stock price.\n\n## SUMMARY\n\nAdvanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD +2.77%) reported record quarterly financial results as the data center segment became the primary contributor to total revenue and earnings. Management raised fiscal 2027 revenue growth expectations to over 80%, citing expanded supply capacity and strengthening demand for AI accelerators and server processors across cloud and enterprise markets. The company is managing a projected double-digit percentage decline in the PC market for 2027 while scaling production for next-generation data center products to meet demand that currently exceeds available supply.\n\n- Su reported that EPYC adoption is expanding across \"cloud, enterprise and super intelligence workloads,\" with data center revenue growth accelerating sequentially every quarter this year.\n- The company began revenue shipments of Venice EPYC processors in the third quarter, with cloud providers planning instance rollouts for early 2027.\n- Management identified agentic workloads as a major compute driver, noting that over 10 million people activated Meta's Muse agents in the first six weeks.\n- The acquisitions of World Labs and Taalas, expected to close by the end of the year, are intended to strengthen spatial intelligence and low-latency inference capabilities.\n- The launch of ROCm 10 introduced ROCm.AI for agentic performance tuning, which management stated reduces weeks of engineering optimization to hours.\n- Su ","highlights":["Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (AMD +2.77%) reported record quarterly financial results as the data center segment became the primary contributor to total revenue and earnings. Management raised fiscal 2027 revenue growth expectations to over 80%, citing expanded supply capacity and strengthening demand for AI accelerators and server processors across cloud and enterprise markets. The company is managing a projected double-digit percentage decline in the PC market for 2027 while scaling production for next-generation data center products to meet demand that currently exceeds available supply.\n\n...\n\nTurning to our data center AI business. Frontier labs, hyperscalers and cloud providers expanded Instinct deployments for inferencing and training driving record revenue. We started shipping MI455X in volume in the quarter, and lead customers, including Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle, brought their first Helios racks online quickly. Customers are now running their latest models and workloads on Helios, and we are seeing very strong performance with the initial deployments. We expect Helios deployments to increase substantially in the fourth quarter as production continues to ramp and HPE, Dell, Lenovo, Super Micro and other OEM and ODM partners begin shipping systems. We are very pleased with the overall performance we are seeing at the rack level.\n\nMI455X leads in compute flops, memory capacity and scale-out bandwidth. And as Helios comes to market, it delivers an even larger lead in memory bandwidth and higher scale-up bandwidth than the competition. We are working closely with our manufacturing and OEM partners to scale production as customers expand their deployments. In supercomputing, EuroHPC selected Instinct MI430X GPUs and 6th Gen EPYC processors for LUMI-AI, Europe's next flagship supercomputer planned to come online in the second half of 2027. MI430X delivers nearly 9x the double precision performance of the competition, which is critical for scientific simulations.\n\n...\n\nFei-Fei Li, brings a world-class research team with expertise in spatial intelligence and models that understand the physical world, giving us deeper insight into how frontier models and workloads are evolving. Fei-Fei will join AMD as Chief Scientist, leading our model research and helping shape our future hardware, software and systems road maps. We expect both acquisitions to close by the end of the year. Looking ahead, our focus is on execution at scale. The racks of Venice, the MI450 Series and Helios are still early, and all 3 are on track to grow significantly. We now expect data center segment revenue growth to accelerate in the fourth quarter and full-year segment revenue to more than double from 2025.\n\nOur visibility into 2027 also continues to strengthen. Last quarter, we said we expected annual server revenue to grow more than 70% and data center segment revenue to more than double for the year. Since then, customers have expanded their EPYC and Instinct deployment plans, and we have secured more supply to support that growth. We now expect server revenue to double year-over-year in 2027 and data center AI revenue to grow even faster than we projected 90 days ago. As a result, we expect data center to be more than 80% of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth.\n\n...\n\nLisa Su: Yes. Sure, Tom. Thanks for the question. So look, we have a lot of momentum going into the fourth quarter and into 2027. We do see a situation where there is very strong demand. So we see demand across the data center business, across our CPU business as well as our data center AI business. And when you look at the rate and pace of that growth, we've been planning for it for the last several years.\n\nSo we've absolutely spent a significant amount of time with our customers planning what their needs are in terms of their deployments and their deployment schedules and also with our supply chain partners to ensure that we have the wafers, the substrates, the advanced packaging, the memory, all of the other components that go along with it. It is true that demand is higher than supply. So we continue to work with our supply chain partners to increase supply. And I do believe that there is a good opportunity for us to do that, just given the strong relationships we have throughout the ecosystem.\n\nBut sitting where we are today to be able to say that the overall company will grow greater than 80%, especially the server business will approximately double from a fairly high point in 2026. And then the data center AI business, we continue to have strong visibility, and we see strong demand from our customers, and we continue to see also good follow-through on all of the other aspects of the infrastructure that are needed. So overall, we're very positive about the data center growth into 2027.\n\n...\n\nLisa Su: Well, Joe, for us to grow that amount, we're meeting a lot of demand. And when you look at -- when we talked about the TAM growing, let's call it, about 50% CAGR over the next 3 or 4 years, we saw growth in sort of 3 areas, right? So traditional cloud and enterprise, agentic, CPUs and agentic workloads and head nodes. We believe we're gaining share in each one of those segments as we give you that forecast of roughly 100%. I do believe there's more demand, and we are actively working with our supply chain partners to satisfy additional demand.\n\nObviously, we also have to make sure that the squared sets are there and DDR5 and all of the other components are there. But my view is we are taking a big step up in terms of the demand forecast from our customers. I'm excited about the fact that our demand is broad-based. So it is really virtually across every customer in terms of their expansion of their footprint with AMD. And so that's positive. And we're going to continue to work on increasing supply to meet additional demand as it comes to fruition."],"summary":"Summary:\n\n- AMD reports record quarterly results driven by the data center segment, with AI accelerators and server processors fueling demand across cloud and enterprise markets.\n- Fiscal 2027: AMD raises revenue growth expectation to over 80%, supported by expanded supply capacity and strong AI workloads; expects data center to be the major revenue driver, potentially >80% of total revenue in 2027.\n- Data center AI: Instinct and MI-series (including MI455X and upcoming Helios systems) driving strong demand.
